newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian railways post 96 loss of 3.6 bln tolars.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian railways post 96 loss of 3.6 bln tolars.

text.p: Slovenian state-owned railway Slovenske Zeleznice (SZ) said on Friday it expected a loss of 3.6 billion tolars ($23.4 million) in 1996 after posting a profit of 68 million tolars in 1995.
"The main reason for the loss is a 15 percent decrease in cargo traffic," Franc Hocevar, deputy executive in charge of economics at SZ, told Reuters.
In 1996 the firm transported 2.6 billion net tonnes per kilometre, down from 3.1 billion a year ago.
The fall in railway cargo to Slovenia was mainly due to high administrative costs, which also caused cargo traffic in Slovenia to move to cheaper trucking, Hocevar noted.
Slovenia's trade with neighbouring Austria, Italy, Croatia and Hungary fell some five percent in 1996.

Hocevar said the company's plans for 1997 largely depended upon expected state help towards maintenance of railway facilities, which will be determined once the 1997 budget is passed by parliament. The budget is due to be adopted by June.
The firm expected to break out of the red this year by reducing administrative costs and modernising its facilities, he added.

In 1997 Slovenian Railways plan to start on the 10 billion tolar construction of a 25 km (15.3 miles) railway between Slovenia and neighbouring Hungary, which currently have no direct rail link between them.

"We are going into the investment together with our neighbours who will have to build some 19 km (11.6 miles) of railway on their side of the border. The construction is expected to be completed by 1999," Hocevar added. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
